resources.string: Tap Race
Everyone taps at once on one screen. First to the finish wins the round.
Race the computer
Race 1 to 3 computer racers. Each one gets a lane of its own.
Same screen
Two to four people race at the same time, each in their own lane. Computers can fill empty lanes.
Race type
Three ways to race on the same screen.
Sprint
Tap as fast as you can. First to fill the track wins.
Rhythm
Tap only on the beat. Early, late and extra taps set you back.
Mash and Brake
Tap fast, but never while the light is red.
The first to win more than half of the rounds takes the match.
Relaxed tapping
Fewer taps to win, wider beat windows and longer red-light warnings, for players who cannot tap fast.
Hold to tap
Hold your pad and it taps for you at a steady pace: a one-button way to play. Not used by Rhythm.
Turn the far lanes around
Players sitting opposite each other read their own lane the right way up. Switch off for one person holding the device.
Tug of War
Pull the marker over your line. Mashing wears you out, so pull smart.
Pull against the computer
Pull against 1 to 3 computer players, alone or with computer team-mates.
Two to four people pull at the same time, each on their own pad. Computers can fill empty pads.
Team layout
How the players pull together. With two players it is always one against one.
Even teams
Two even teams: 2 against 2 with four players, 1 against 2 with three.
One against the rest
One player pulls against everyone else, up to 1 against 3.
Free for all
Everybody pulls for themselves toward their own corner.
Relaxed pulling
Mashing tires you less, heaves charge faster and rounds last longer, for players who cannot pull fast.
Hold to pull
Hold your pad and it pulls for you at a steady pace: a one-button way to play.
Turn the far side around
Players sitting opposite each other read their own pad the right way up. Switch off for one person holding the device.
